meta.title: Toronto priorities survey
meta.intro: Where should the next council put its money, its powers and its attention? Your answers shape what we push candidates on before Toronto votes on October 26.

thankYou.title: Thank you. Your answers are in.
thankYou.body: We read every response. Results will be published ward by ward before the campaign period opens.

questions.label: Postal code
Which ward do you live in?
How long have you lived here?
If Toronto could make one major housing intervention this term, which should receive the greatest emphasis?

options.label: Permission
options.detail: Permit substantially more housing as-of-right

options.label: Cost and speed
options.detail: Reduce approval times, development charges and other city-imposed costs

options.label: Public delivery
options.detail: Build or finance substantially more affordable and supportive housing

questions.label: What should be Toronto's primary role in delivering affordable and supportive housing?

options.label: Direct provider
options.detail: Build, acquire and own significantly more housing

options.label: Partner and financier
options.detail: Supply land, funding and incentives to non-profit and private providers

options.label: Regulator and enabler
options.detail: Focus primarily on permitting enough housing and reducing barriers to construction

questions.label: Where should Toronto permit the greatest increase in housing density?

options.label: Across the city
options.detail: Permit more apartments and multiplexes in nearly every neighbourhood

options.label: Along corridors and transit
options.detail: Concentrate growth on major streets and near rapid transit

options.label: In designated centres
options.detail: Concentrate most growth downtown and in existing growth centres

questions.label: What should receive the greatest share of the next available transit funding?

options.label: Service
options.detail: More frequent and reliable service on existing routes

options.label: Maintenance
options.detail: Vehicles, stations, signals and other state-of-good-repair work

options.label: Expansion
options.detail: New rapid-transit lines and extensions

questions.label: When there is not enough street space for every use, which should generally receive priority?

options.label: Passenger capacity
options.detail: Transit, walking and cycling

options.label: Goods and essential access
options.detail: Deliveries, trades, emergency vehicles and accessibility

options.label: General traffic and parking
options.detail: Automobile capacity and curbside parking

questions.label: If large-scale autonomous taxi service is introduced in Toronto, what should the city regulate most aggressively?

options.label: Safety
options.detail: Collision standards and interaction with pedestrians, cyclists and other road users

options.label: Street use
options.detail: Congestion, empty vehicles, pickups and curb access

options.label: Public obligations
options.detail: Accessibility, geographic coverage and service standards

questions.label: Which approach should receive the greatest additional investment to improve public safety?

options.label: Enforcement
options.detail: Police, bylaw enforcement and a more visible official presence

options.label: Crisis and prevention services
options.detail: Mental-health response, addiction treatment and youth intervention

options.label: Public-space management
options.detail: Lighting, maintenance, sanitation and active use of streets and parks

questions.label: Over the next council term, the Toronto Police Service budget should:

options.label: Increase above inflation to expand police staffing or services
Decrease after inflation, with some responsibilities and funding transferred to civilian services

questions.label: How should Toronto govern automated licence-plate readers and similar surveillance technology used on public streets?

options.label: Permit broad use
options.detail: Allow police and approved organizations to deploy them under existing privacy law

options.label: Permit under strict rules
options.detail: Establish citywide limits on access, retention, auditing and data sharing

options.label: Prohibit broad automated collection
options.detail: Restrict their use to narrowly authorized investigations

questions.label: Which change would do the most to reduce the cost of building housing in Toronto?

options.label: Lower municipal charges
options.detail: Reduce development charges, parkland payments and related levies

options.label: Faster approvals
options.detail: Expand as-of-right zoning and automate routine permits

options.label: Simpler standards
options.detail: Reduce parking, design and other construction requirements

questions.label: What is the most important change Toronto should make to reduce capital-project delays and cost overruns?

options.label: Improve project delivery
options.detail: Strengthen professional project management, procurement and contracting

options.label: Control political changes
options.detail: Prevent councillors from altering scope after approval without identifying funding

options.label: Limit the project pipeline
options.detail: Start fewer projects and fully fund them before construction begins

questions.label: Which service-delivery model should Toronto use more often?

options.label: Direct delivery
options.detail: Expand permanent city staff and internal operational capacity

options.label: External delivery
options.detail: Use competitive contracts and outside providers where they can deliver better value

options.label: Specialized agencies
options.detail: Move major functions to arm's-length organizations with clear performance mandates

questions.label: Over the next council term, residential property-tax revenues should generally:

options.label: Grow faster than inflation to improve or expand services
Grow approximately with inflation and population
Grow more slowly than inflation, requiring service restraint or alternative revenues

questions.label: Which type of additional revenue should Toronto rely on most heavily?

options.label: Broad recurring revenue
options.detail: Property taxes or new municipal income or sales taxes, if authorized

options.label: Growth and transaction revenue
options.detail: Land-transfer taxes, development charges and taxes on real-estate activity

options.label: User and road charges
options.detail: Congestion charges, tolls, parking levies and service fees

questions.label: What should Toronto do first to address its infrastructure repair backlog?

options.label: Raise dedicated revenue
options.detail: Introduce a levy or other recurring source reserved for maintenance

options.label: Delay expansion
options.detail: Redirect money from new facilities and projects toward existing assets

options.label: Reduce the asset base
options.detail: Sell, consolidate or close facilities the city cannot sustainably maintain

questions.label: What should be Toronto's primary approach to the provincial government?

options.label: Partnership
options.detail: Align with provincial priorities where doing so secures funding or approvals

options.label: Advocacy
options.detail: Publicly press for greater authority, revenue and a different fiscal arrangement

options.label: Self-reliance
options.detail: Plan budgets and services on the assumption that substantial new provincial support will not arrive

questions.label: Over the next council term, Toronto should:

options.label: Accelerate
options.detail: Expand the protected cycling network, including projects that remove traffic lanes or parking

options.label: Complete existing commitments
options.detail: Finish approved projects but undertake few additional road reallocations

options.label: Review and reverse
options.detail: Remove or redesign lanes that fail defined safety, ridership or congestion standards

options.label: Maintaining access
options.detail: Keep major roads, transit, hospitals and essential facilities operating

options.label: Protecting protest
options.detail: Accept significant disruption unless there is an immediate safety threat

options.label: Predetermined limits
options.detail: Protect protest subject to clear rules for locations, access routes and duration

options.label: Internal operations
options.detail: Procurement, finance, staffing and administrative efficiency

options.label: Performance management
options.detail: Public data and systems that measure outcomes and hold departments accountable

options.label: Reduce internal administration, staffing or contract costs
Raise taxes, fees or other revenue

questions.label: What is the most important municipal intervention for improving Toronto's business climate?

options.label: Lower costs
options.detail: Reduce commercial taxes, fees and licensing expenses

options.label: Reduce delay
options.detail: Accelerate permits, inspections and approvals

options.label: Improve fundamentals
options.detail: Expand housing, transportation, public safety and infrastructure

questions.label: How should Toronto attract major employers, investment and events?

options.label: Targeted incentives
options.detail: Direct financial bids, tax measures or customized agreements

options.label: Citywide fundamentals
options.detail: Housing affordability, transportation, safety and quality of life

options.label: Sector strategy
options.detail: Concentrate resources on a small number of industries where Toronto has an existing advantage

questions.step_intro: All optional. Skip any you don't have a view on.
questions.label: What should Toronto prioritize to increase construction capacity?

options.label: Predictable demand
options.detail: Maintain a stable, long-term pipeline of public projects

options.label: Workforce supply
options.detail: Expand apprenticeships, training and recognition of international credentials

options.label: Productivity
options.detail: Encourage modular construction, prefabrication and more efficient building methods

questions.label: What should receive the greatest priority in Toronto's public-realm budget?

options.label: Basic maintenance
options.detail: Cleanliness, roads, sidewalks, snow clearing, washrooms and routine park care

options.label: Major improvements
options.detail: A smaller number of transformative parks, streets and public spaces

options.label: Programming and activity
options.detail: Markets, events, patios, recreation and cultural programming

questions.label: What should be Toronto's primary tool for supporting arts, culture and nightlife?

options.label: Regulatory reform
options.detail: Simpler permits, flexible operating rules and later hours

options.label: Public funding
options.detail: Grants, city facilities and affordable cultural space

options.label: Protection from displacement
options.detail: Planning and property measures that preserve existing venues and workspaces

questions.step_title: A few more, if you have time

questions.label: If autonomous taxi services operate in Toronto, which condition should the city prioritize?

options.label: Data disclosure
options.detail: Mandatory reporting on trips, collisions, congestion and curb use

options.label: Service obligations
options.detail: Accessibility, geographic coverage and minimum service standards

options.label: Limited municipal conditions
options.detail: Avoid additional requirements beyond provincial regulation
